title: Kidnapper
text: “Fu fu fu, now that’s an interesting thing to say.”
That was a mocking sort of laugh from Rabbit Guy, different from the kind Keel gave.
“There is absolutely no possibility of that. Naofumi-sama is not the sort of person who would do such a thing. I’d actually like to ask how he would even go about committing rape.”
“He could easily just attack her, couldn’t he!? Are you saying you can doubt him even after seeing Myne-san’s tears?”

The Crimson Swine’s tears were fake, falser than garbage, indeed. Slaughtering it would almost be too kind—the only real question was how to dispose of the Crimson Swine this time in the most miserable way possible.
“If Father were violated by a pig, it’d be Father who ended up damaged and defiled, I say. There’s no way he’d ever do such a thing.”
Oops. I’d meant not to say that out loud, but it slipped out anyway.
“Motoyasu-kun!”
“Not a chance. The more I come to know Naofumi-sama’s character, the more certain I am it’s impossible. In fact, let me say it plainly—if anything, he’d be the one at risk of being violated!”
Rabbit Guy clenched his fists with all his might—oh, he got so worked up his hands turned into rabbit paws. Though apparently painless, judging by how fluffy they looked.
“Wh— hold on—”
“The way he goes out walking around alone… it worries me terribly. What if he’s caught by some brutish soldier or adventurer somewhere and meets a horrible fate?”
The mongrel lizardman stayed silent through Rabbit Guy’s passionate speech, but crossed his arms and nodded along in agreement.

“Judging from his usual demeanor and how he treats people, it’s simply impossible. In fact, I’ll go further—being desired by a Hero should be an honor. Even setting that aside, he’s hardly the type anyone could convincingly play victim against. The whole premise is absurd!”
Thwip! Rabbit Guy pointed one fluffy-turned finger straight at Itsuki.
“Wha— And yet Myne-san still couldn’t accept it! What is wrong with you!? Defending him makes you just as guilty!”
“Say whatever you like. I’ve simply judged that you aren’t worth believing.”
“Theo, Shion! Don’t provoke him too much, nothing good’ll come of it… especially you, Theo! Who said anything about anyone getting raped?”
“How shameless can you get… There are rumors of misdeeds happening all over the place. I’d rather not see Heroes fighting amongst themselves.”
Misdeeds all over the place—probably some fake rumor going around using Father’s name, I’d wager.
For some reason, Father fell silent. Wasn’t he going to argue back?
“I have absolutely no memory of any such thing.”
“How brazen. There are rumors you’re running some sort of human trafficking circus!”
Ah, so that’s what this was about. All I was doing was capturing the Three Heroes Church zealots who kept attacking us and shipping them off to other countries.
“If even the slightest wrongdoing had come to light, wouldn’t we not even be standing here right now?”

“Wherever we go, we get audited constantly, and there is absolutely no truth whatsoever to any kidnapping, I say. Itsuki, you should understand that it’s because of rumors spread by people like you that I’ve been forced into this line of work in the first place, indeed. The audits come so often it’s practically nitpicking. We’ve barely just started, and they show up almost daily.”

Huh? Father made a face at that, but it didn’t really need to be true. Since Father was already being denied his duties as a Hero, his work, and use of the Guild, it wasn’t exactly a lie either. Kidnapping? All I was doing was dealing with bandits who attacked us. Just selling off the sparks that fell on me, so to speak. After all, there’s no law saying bandits must be captured alive. No one gets punished for disposing of them. At most, if you catch one, you’re expected to haul them to a guard post. Which meant, as far as we were concerned, our bandit “processing” counted as subjugation. Calling it a crime was a stretch. Of course, the actual truth was that we sold them to Siltvelt.
“Isn’t it rather a problem to go digging for dirt where there is none, and spread baseless rumors, I say?”
We were just having other countries deal justice to bandits our own country refused to punish properly.
“Well, they could just repent, couldn’t they?”
“Oh? By Itsuki’s reasoning, do criminals get to walk into respectable jobs the moment they reform, I wonder?”
“Th—”
Oh? Itsuki, about to snap back, fell into an awkward silence instead.
“It’s their own fault for becoming criminals in the first place!”
“There’s no reasoning with you, I say.”
“Regardless, being accused of something I have no memory of leaves me no choice but to say I don’t know anything about it, I say.”
“How shameless.”

Father wore an expression of utter exasperation. Itsuki in this state was, as ever, incredibly obnoxious. Well, honestly, Itsuki after learning the truth was obnoxious too. Whenever I called him Nyu-Nanbu, he’d relentlessly try to snipe me for it.
“And you think condemning someone based on a predetermined conclusion counts as justice? What clouded eyes you must have.”
Rabbit Guy sneered at Itsuki as if shielding Father.
“What’s so funny!? Stop looking at me like that! It’s disgusting!”

“Then perhaps you ought to listen to Naofumi-sama’s side a little more. From what I’ve seen so far, you haven’t been listening to him at all. Isn’t the truth more likely to reveal itself by hearing both sides?”

Itsuki and Rabbit Guy glared at each other with crackling intensity. Now that I thought about it, Rabbit Guy was the one who’d gotten furious that I hadn’t helped Father while Itsuki went along with the false accusations. Back then, since Father hadn’t said much himself, Rabbit Guy had apparently tagged along with lingering suspicion, only to realize the truth during the duel and erupt in anger. Regardless, it was clear Itsuki and Rabbit Guy simply didn’t mesh well. That reminded me—Riska had once said, while trying to persuade Itsuki, that the opposite of one justice is simply another justice. In other words, Itsuki’s justice and Rabbit Guy’s justice were colliding head-on.

“In any case, you’re getting off topic. The issue is that this country refuses Class Ups to demi-humans and beastmen in the first place. Isn’t obstructing a Hero trying to face the Waves putting the cart before the horse?”
“Giving power to the companions of a criminal Hero is something only a fool would do!”

“There you go again, circling back. I’m telling you, it’s about time you saw with your own eyes what kind of country this really is. Blaming someone is easy, and it feels good, doesn’t it? If you’re truly a Hero, shouldn’t you be capable of some compassion?”
It was obvious at a glance that Itsuki was growing irritated with Rabbit Guy, who refused to back down even an inch.
“Ugh… how long do you two intend to keep up this pointless bickering?”
Ren, thoroughly fed up with the exchange, pushed Kuro-chan’s head—who’d been clinging to him—out of the way and stepped between the two of them.
“If you want to fight, do it later. I need to get my companions their Class Ups.”
“Ren-san! Are you saying you agree with Naofumi-san too!?”
“That shady little farce? How long do you intend to keep obsessing over something so pointless?”
“……Ugh, enough already. You’re noisy.”
The mongrel lizardman, sounding thoroughly exasperated, grabbed Rabbit Guy from behind and lifted him up.
“Wah! Shion, what are you doing!”
“Stop bothering Shield Hero. Look.”

When the mongrel lizardman pointed at Father, Father wore a wry smile. No—if my memory served correctly, it was a smile laced with quiet fury. No doubt he was furious about that comment regarding being the one violated. Yuki-chan and I had managed to dodge the lecture that was surely coming our way, but Rabbit Guy had gone and stepped right on the landmine instead. Whether he’d come to his senses or simply sensed the mood, Rabbit Guy’s face had gone a touch pale.
“Let’s go, now.”
At Ren’s words, his companions followed after him.
“Yep. Let’s go, Dark Saint Hero.”
“You’re not coming.”

As Kuro-chan tried to tag along as though it were the most natural thing in the world, Ren rejected him while turning his gaze toward—not me, but Father. Was that his roundabout way of asking for help?
“Kuro-chan, I know you want to cling to Ren, but later, okay?”
“Not later! Motoyasu!”
“Time to awaken as the Dark Saint Hero, I say.”
“Shut up! What is that even supposed to mean!? Just keep him restrained already!”
“Kuro’s got, like, pitch-black fangs and claws, y’know—”

Utterly indifferent to the wind blowing around him, Kuro-chan kept right on clinging to Ren. Even Ren’s companions seemed at a loss, unable to push back too hard against Kuro-chan’s obvious attachment to him. Well, I’m sure Kuro-chan and Ren will get along eventually. It’s only a matter of time before he’s fully active as the Dark Saint Hero.
“If he adores you this much, there’s nothing to be done. I’ll leave Kuro-chan in your care, I say.”
“Don’t just decide that on your own! Take him back!”
“Kuro-chan.”
“Booo… until fate crosses our paths again, this is a brief farewell—”
Ren walked off as Kuro-chan waved his hand, clearly thrown off his rhythm. For what it’s worth, Ren’s eyebrow twitched slightly. Hard to say whether that meant he was pleased or annoyed.
